newsitem.title: USA: Dow resumes run, flirts with 6400 as IBM roars on.
newsitem.headline: Dow resumes run, flirts with 6400 as IBM roars on.

text.p: The Dow industrials jumped back onto the record-smashing track as dynamo International Business Machines Corp reached skyward and bond yields pressed lower on further signs of a weakening economy.

"What a great tape...It's the most powerful bull market of all time and has the horses to go higher. The true leadership is Microsoft, Intel and IBM. It feels like '85 and '86. The market wants to go somewhere and it has to travel a lot of points to get there," said James Cramer of Cramer Co.
The Dow surged 50 to about 6398 after flirting with 6400.

It was the Dow's 40th record closing high for 1996 and its ninth record out of the past 10 trading sessions. The blue chip index slipped one point Monday after rallying more than 350 points the previous two weeks.
IBM rallied 6-3/4 to 153-3/4, climbing nearly 20 points since last Thursday.
Microsoft surged 5-1/2 to 155-7/8 and Intel climbed 5-3/8 to 120-3/4, helping the Nasdaq Composite up eight to 1263.
The S&P 500 rose five to about 742, topping the previous record close of 737.62 set last Friday. The NYSE Composite added two to 392, also topping Friday's record 390.02.
Winners beat losers 7-5 on very heavy NYSE volume of about 455 million shares.

The long bond rose 14/32, sending its yield down to 6.44 percent from 6.47 percent on Monday. Bonds firmed and equities followed after news October housing starts fell 5.1 percent to an annualized 1.366 million rate, the lowest since October 1995's 1.351 million rate. A 1.443 million unit rate was seen.

"The bond's going to six percent, so you're not making money there," Cramer said. "The consumer domestic economy is slowing down. But the corporate domestic economy is fine and and the international corporate economy is also doing well."

The company reported fiscal fourth-quarter earnings of $0.62 a share, missing the Street's consensus by two pennies. Hewlett-Packard said orders grew 15 percent from a year ago, compared with an eight percent rise in the third quarter.
Bay Networks added 1-5/8 to 25-1/2. Prudential upgraded Bay to buy, raised earnings estimates and its price target.
Compaq rose four to 80-3/8 after a senior executive forecast a strong first half 1997 at the Comdex trade show in Las Vegas.
CompUSA lost 4-1/8 to 44-3/4. Montgomery Securities downgraded the stock to hold from buy.
